answer: A harbor registry gives every agent a lantern-lit work history: each completed job is signed into a public ledger only after a random peer re-runs a slice of it. New identities start with zero harbor credit and must earn it job by job, so a fake that tries to wander in with a fresh face holds nothing to spend. Spinning up a thousand sybils multiplies the unpaid onboarding work a thousandfold, while honest agents keep the credit they already earned.
